publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic-Aided Current-Limiting Circuit Breaker Developments and Applications
IEE Colloquium on Electronic-Aided Current-Limiting Circuit Breaker Developments and Applications
abstract: There has been growing interest in the GTO circuit breakers for electric railways. The GTO circuit breaker features high speed interrupting capability and hybrid analog/digital control. This provides short interrupting times when short-circuit faults occur close to the substation and also gives precise overload protection of the circuit breaker itself. The electromagnetic energy trapped in the circuit inductance is dissipated in the energy absorber. A zinc oxide varistor, showing a sharp nonlinear voltage-current characteristic, provides a desirable property as the energy absorber. The author discussed the main features of the GTO circuit breaker.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fast DC hybrid circuit breaker
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic-Aided Current-Limiting Circuit Breaker Developments and Applications
abstract: The authors briefly discuss the problems of the classical interruption technique used in DC circuit breakers. They then describe a prototype hybrid thyristor circuit breaker which utilises the principle of counter-current to effect current interruption. The operation of the circuit breaker is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic-Aided Current-Limiting Circuit Breaker Developments and Applications
abstract: Thyristor-based circuit breakers are very simple devices. In essence they interrupt current by either injecting a counter-current from a pre-charged capacitance source into the cathode terminal of SCR devices or into the gate terminals of GTO devices. The author discusses these current interruption techniques, the switching overvoltages, and the operating principles.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A thyristor circuit breaker for ship protection
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic-Aided Current-Limiting Circuit Breaker Developments and Applications
abstract: A semiconductor short-circuit current limiting set (S-CLS) developed in Gdansk was designed for application in AC low voltage power systems with an insulated neutral point. This configuration is widely used for example on ships or coal mine electrical networks. This S-CLS is based on the Schulze-Buxloh system. The concept of the S-CLS set consists of a special connection of the neutral point of a generator or transformer. The neutral point contains a 3-phase rectifier or half controlled bridge, in which a current limiting thyristor circuit-breaker (TCB), with current commutation, shunts the DC side. In the case of a short-circuit in the circuits supplied by the generator or transformer, the TCB operates, disconnecting the DC branch of the neutral point. The operation is equivalent to interruption of the short-circuit current on the AC side. Tests were performed at the Electrotechnical Institute, the Gdansk Branch, on the S-CLS normal working conditions and during short-circuits. Some selected test results characterising the most important features of the S-CLS are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Thyristor circuit breaker devices for energy recovery applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic-Aided Current-Limiting Circuit Breaker Developments and Applications
abstract: An auxiliary switched thyristor circuit breaker (TCB) with a switching free-wheel diode was developed to overcome some special problems when protecting an AC line commutated thyristor inverter fed from a large 'lumped' inductive DC supply. The particular application to which an 1800 A/750 V TCB has been applied, was to provide fast acting overcurrent protection on the DC side of a regenerative test circuit for continuous load testing of diesel-electric shunting locomotive engines, rated up to 600 kW. The inverter was used to recover 70-80% of the energy normally dissipated during the tests. The power delivered in the inverter mode typically being 200-500 kW, could be used locally to reduce the peak power demand on the local AC system. The energy saving was estimated to be 450000 kWh/year.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Two-stage thyristor circuit breaker short circuit characteristics
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic-Aided Current-Limiting Circuit Breaker Developments and Applications
abstract: A two-stage thyristor circuit breaker (TCB) has been developed by British industry in conjunction with academia. The principal differences between the two-stage TCB and other types, is that is dissipates the energy stored in circuits during load switching, or fault clearance, in a controlled manner, using switched inserted resistance. The technique enables limitation of the switching voltage to twice the system voltage (2 pu) for practical systems, and permits optimisation of the ratings and cost of the TCB circuit components. A compact, withdrawable, prototype design, rated nominally at 4000 A, 700 V DC, has been extensively tested under a variety of short-circuit test conditions. The prototype TCB successfully cleared a range of fault conditions, typical of mass rapid transit systems. In all cases the overvoltage was limited to 2 Pu, as predicted by simulation studies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic-Aided Current-Limiting Circuit Breaker Developments and Applications
abstract: Current interruption requires that a 'part' of the circuit ideally switches from a conducting state, to an insulating one. This operation can be achieved by an electric arc appearing between separating contacts, but semiconductors are also able to undergo this transition. The authors present research that has been performed at the University of Liege, in order to develop hybrid circuit breakers. These devices combine both interrupting solutions: separating contacts and semiconductors. This technique avoids the drawbacks existing when using only one of them. The authors discuss both AC and DC current interruption using these thyristor based circuit breakers. The main features and advantages are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
